English: Timber Belfry
A simple wooden scaffolding, quickly erected by frontier monks to house a single bell and call the faithful to prayer.
Stone Bell Platform
A sturdy stone base replaces the wooden frame, providing a more lasting structure for the temple bell and marking the settlements growing permanence.
Double Bell Chamber
An expanded stone tower with two tuned bells, allowing for richer chimes that mark holy days and summon the faithful from greater distances.
Single Bell Tower
A tall, narrow tower with a single bronze bell, visible from afar and symbolizing spiritual stability for the community.
Reinforced Tower
Thickened walls and buttresses protect the bells and provide a defensible position for the clergy in times of upheaval.
Clockwork Mechanism
Sophisticated clockwork machinery automates the ringing of bells for prayer, discipline, and timekeeping, inspiring awe in the devout and visitors alike.
Triple Bell Array
A trio of harmonized bells, each rung in sequence by clockwork, resounds across the countryside, reinforcing the temples influence and prestige.
Carillon Tower
A grand tower housing a full carillon, its music ringing out with intricate melodies for ceremonies, festivals, and royal visits.
Cathedral Bell Tower
A monumental structure, visible for miles, whose complex bell system marks the most sacred moments in the realms spiritual life.
Great Resonance Tower
The ultimate bell tower, its massive bells and ingenious mechanisms inspire awe, drawing pilgrims from across the land and making the temple a center of faith and power.
